strategy_title: Halve BLOCK_K to reduce shared memory bank conflicts
strategy_description: When a Triton GEMM kernel exhibits high shared memory bank conflict rates (>80% of wavefronts are conflict wavefronts, >15-way average conflict) due to a large BLOCK_K tile, halving BLOCK_K (e.g. 64→32) reduces the shared memory staging footprint and lowers the bank conflict multiplier. In this case, halving BLOCK_K from 64 to 32 reduced warp cycles per issued instruction from 7.9 to 2.96 (2.7x improvement) and cut kernel duration from 23.23 µs to 17.18 µs (1.35x speedup), while also relaxing the shared memory block limit from 4 to 6 blocks/SM. Pairing this with @triton.autotune over num_warps and num_stages allows the runtime to select the best latency-hiding configuration for the reduced tile geometry.
applicable_when: Triton GEMM kernel with SharedMemoryConflicts rule triggered; average bank conflict way >10; conflict wavefronts >70% of total; warp cycles per issued instruction >5 due to MIO stalls; BLOCK_K is a power-of-2 ≥64; kernel is memory-bound at L1/TEX (throughput >80%)
do_not_apply_when: BLOCK_K is already ≤32; K dimension is not divisible by the reduced BLOCK_K without adding boundary masking; reducing BLOCK_K would increase the number of loop iterations to the point of compute becoming the bottleneck; occupancy is already high (>50%) and bank conflicts are mild (<5-way)
framework_notes: In Triton, BLOCK_K is a tl.constexpr tile parameter controlling the shared memory staging size for the K-reduction loop in GEMM. Halving it halves the shared memory per block, which relaxes the Block Limit Shared Mem constraint and can increase theoretical occupancy. The @triton.autotune decorator with varying num_warps and num_stages is used to find the best software-pipelining depth for the new tile geometry. Equivalent in CUDA: reduce the tile K dimension in the shared memory declaration and loop unroll factor.

strategy_title: Replace broadcast_to B load with direct pointer arithmetic
strategy_description: When a Triton GEMM kernel loads the B matrix using tl.broadcast_to with intermediate index variables (idx_m, idx_n, xindex), replacing this with direct pointer arithmetic (b_ptrs = B + (offs_k[:,None] + k_base) + stride_n * offs_n[None,:]) eliminates unnecessary compiler overhead and intermediate variable reuse. In this case, the refactor yielded a modest 1.36x speedup (duration 17.18→17.02 µs) despite the SharedMemoryConflicts rule remaining active at the same severity (13.2-way, 79.67% conflict wavefronts), suggesting the gain came from reduced instruction count (1,839,090→1,832,448 executed instructions) rather than bank conflict elimination. The bank conflict pattern persisted because the root cause (stride-192 access with 192 mod 32 = 0) was not fully resolved by the pointer arithmetic change alone — the shared memory staging inside tl.dot still serializes conflicting accesses.
slow_pseudocode:
# Inside k_idx loop — uses broadcast_to and intermediate variables
a_k_idx_vals = offs_k[None, :] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)
b_k_idx_vals = offs_k[:, None] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)
idx_m = offs_a_m[:, None]
idx_n = a_k_idx_vals
xindex = idx_n + 192*idx_m
a = tl.load(A + xindex)
idx_m = b_k_idx_vals
idx_n = offs_b_n[None, :]
xindex = idx_n + 32*idx_m
b = tl.load(B + tl.broadcast_to(idx_m + 192*idx_n, [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]))
acc += tl.dot(a, b)
fast_pseudocode:
# Inside k_idx loop — direct pointer arithmetic, no broadcast_to
k_base = k_idx * BLOCK_K
a_ptrs = A + offs_a_m[:, None] * 192 + (offs_k[None, :] + k_base)
a = tl.load(a_ptrs)
b_ptrs = B + (offs_k[:, None] + k_base) + 192 * offs_b_n[None, :]
b = tl.load(b_ptrs)
acc += tl.dot(a, b)
applicable_when: Triton GEMM kernel uses tl.broadcast_to or multi-step intermediate index variables (idx_m, idx_n, xindex) to compute load addresses inside the K-reduction loop; SharedMemoryConflicts rule is active; instruction count is elevated due to redundant index arithmetic; registers per thread are high (>120) suggesting compiler spill or variable reuse overhead.
do_not_apply_when: The kernel already uses direct pointer arithmetic for all loads; the bank conflict root cause is a stride that is a multiple of the number of shared memory banks (e.g. stride mod 32 == 0) — in that case, direct pointer arithmetic alone will not eliminate the bank conflicts and a padding or transposition strategy is needed instead; the broadcast_to is semantically necessary for correctness (e.g. non-uniform shapes).
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.broadcast_to can introduce extra compiler-visible intermediate tensors that inflate register usage and instruction count. Replacing it with explicit 2D pointer arithmetic (row_offsets[:,None] * stride_row + col_offsets[None,:] * stride_col) is idiomatic and allows the compiler to optimize the address computation more aggressively. Note: this change does NOT fix bank conflicts caused by strides that are multiples of 32 (the number of shared memory banks) — those require padding the shared memory allocation or transposing the tile layout.

applicable_when: The B matrix has stride_bn=192 (N-major stride). When tl.dot stages the [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] B tile into shared memory, consecutive rows are separated by 192 elements x 4 bytes = 768 bytes = 24 x 32-byte bank-widths. Since 192 mod 32 = 0, every row of the B tile maps to the same set of banks, causing maximum bank conflicts (17.9-way average, 83% conflict wavefronts). Prior attempts (BLOCK_K reduction, pointer arithmetic refactor, B-matrix transposition) all left 13.2-way conflicts intact because they did not change the fundamental stride-mod-32=0 alignment. The canonical fix is to pad the shared memory staging buffer by 8 elements in the K dimension (BLOCK_K_PAD = BLOCK_K + 8 = 40), so row i starts at bank (i*40) mod 32 = (i*8) mod 32, cycling through {0,8,16,24} across 4 rows instead of all landing on bank 0. TF32 is kept False because it previously caused correctness failure (max_diff ~5e-2 > atol=1e-3).
